title: ClimateAR: Multi-Scale Autoregressive Generative Modeling for Climate Forecasting
claim: A two-stage system, a multi-scale residual tokenizer plus a causal transformer conditioned on mixed-scale tokens, turns past states into probabilistic forecasts.
layout: 2 panels, left tokenizer and right AR transformer, bottom-to-top flow
description: A dashed vertical line splits the figure into (a) Tokenizer on the left and (b) AR Transformer on the right. Panel (a) shows climate-field images fed through CNN encoders, a label-switch node S, and an Encoder. A yellow rounded box expands the quantizer into residual stages (f, res1, res2) with Down, Look-up and Up blocks and subtraction/addition nodes. These stages produce token grids r1, r2 and r3 of growing size in blue, and a Decoder reconstructs the fields. Panel (b) is a larger diagram. Tokenizers turn X_t and X_{t+1} into per-scale token rows (Scale 1, 2, K). Orange mixed-token embedding, a yellow hybrid-scale cross-attention and prompt tokens feed a grey Causal Transformer. Arrows run up to the predicted tokens, a CE loss and a Decoder that outputs X_pred. Color codes token types: blue targets, orange mixed tokens, grey predictions.

abstract: Accurate climate forecasting provides critical support for decision-making in agriculture, energy, and disaster preparedness. Current deterministic models often fail to capture climate uncertainty, while existing generative approaches oversimplify the system by neglecting key spatiotemporal dependencies and cross-scale interactions. To address these limitations, we introduce ClimateAR, an AutoRegressive generative model for probabilistic seasonal-to-interannual Climate forecasting. The framework incorporates two novel components: (1) an aligned tokenizer that bridges and aligns heterogeneous simulation and real-world data to improve transferability across domains, and (2) a mixed-scale conditioning mechanism that captures multi-scale climate interactions for robust probabilistic forecasting. Extensive evaluations on the ERA5 reanalysis dataset show that ClimateAR achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving anomaly correlation skill by 37.56\% on average compared to leading baselines.
